Title: Diagnosis

Details: The issue reported states that getParsedOptionValue returns null unless Option.type is explicitly set, but users expect the type to default to String if not set otherwise. Inspecting the failing test and the OptionBuilder usage confirms this expectation from users.

Examining the OptionBuilder methods involved in the test from lines 43-49 and 59-62 shows it uses withType(Float.class) explicitly setting the type in the first Option, but not in the second Option (lines 59-62). The test then asserts that the second Option's type is String (line 67), implying a default type should be String if none is set.

Looking into OptionBuilder.create(String), this method creates an Option using new Option(opt, description) constructor, then sets properties like longOpt, required, args, type, etc. The critical part is option.setType(type), where type is a static field in OptionBuilder that presumably retains the type set last or null if never set.

The Option(String, String) constructor calls Option(String opt, String longOpt, boolean hasArg, String description) with longOpt null and hasArg false as default, but does not set a type anywhere in these constructors.

Therefore, the likely problem is that Option.type is not initialized to String by default in either the Option constructor or in OptionBuilder. Instead, it's left unset (null) unless explicitly set with withType(...). This causes getParsedOptionValue to return null for options without explicit type set.

Hence, the root cause is the absence of a default type assignment (to String.class) in the Option class or in the OptionBuilder when type is not explicitly set. The failure in testTwoCompleteOptions reflects this, because in the second Option created with OptionBuilder, type remains null but the test expects it to be String.class.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report proposal to either fix this in the Option constructor or in CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue, or at least document it clearly in Option.

Recent bug reports about inconsistencies in Option constructors do not directly help with this type defaulting issue, so can be disregarded here.

Summary: Option.type does not default to String.class causing getParsedOptionValue to return null unless set explicitly via OptionBuilder.withType(...). This causes the failing test assertion expecting String.class as default type.

The best fix locations are the Option constructor(s) to set a default type of String.class or OptionBuilder.create(...) to default the static type field to String.class if unset before calling option.setType(type).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
